summary.intent: Capture a discovered design issue (folder-state ownership split between web store and SDK client) as a tracked todo and open a PR to preserve it durably, separate from the active bugfix PR #489.
summary.outcome: Todo file created at `.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-14-unify-folder-state-ownership-in-sdk-client.md`, committed on an isolated branch, PR #490 opened, and the branch merged into main (fast-forward, 188 lines added across 4 files).

repo: The project uses `.planning/todos/pending/` as a structured todo store with markdown files named by date and slug.
Todos are cross-linked when related but kept separate when scopes differ — CAS retry-loop dedup and folder state ownership are distinct concerns despite both touching the SDK.
The repo has a `release-please` automation branch (`release-please--branches--main`) that receives forced updates alongside normal main merges.
PRs are opened for todo/planning captures (not just code changes) to make them durable and tracked in GitHub.

code.finding: New todo capturing design: SDK client should be single source of truth for folder state; web store becomes a projection fed by `folder:updated` events; exit criterion is deletion of `reconcileFolderState`.
Modified as part of the folder-state ownership capture — 23 lines changed (+6 net), likely annotating the bypass paths or adding TODOs inline.
59 new lines of tests added alongside the capture, suggesting test scaffolding or failing tests were committed to document the expected future behavior.
35 new lines added — likely stubs or inline TODO markers for the SDK client becoming the authoritative folder-state owner.

workflow: Isolating captures/todos on their own branch and opening a PR keeps planning artifacts out of active bugfix PRs and ensures they survive in git history.
The `/gsd:capture` command produces structured todo files with metadata (area, severity, referenced files) and handles branch/PR creation automatically.
Cross-linking related todos requires a manual check to confirm scopes are truly distinct before keeping them separate.
